judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Effective Date is left as "July ¥, 2005" — the operative date on which the Employment Term, Restricted Period and severance run-off all depend is illegible/blank, a mechanical defect visible on the face of the recital. "Company" is also defined to mean two entities jointly, which makes every later "the Company shall" obligation ambiguous as to which entity owes it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The collective "Company" definition sits awkwardly against 2.2(a), 2.2(e), 8.2, 8.4 and 8.5, which assign payment obligations specifically to "Ajuba India" while other clauses say "the Company shall pay"; the missing date also unsettles 1.9 and 8.1 (third anniversary of the Effective Date). Still, the parties and the basic bargain are identifiable, so the incoherence is limited.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-line definition tying "Board" to a single named corporation's board; nothing in the words is capable of two readings.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 has the Employee reporting to the Board "or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent," and 8.4(b) speaks of Parent removing him from "the Board," so the defined term does some odd work, but no direct conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The definition is built on two open-ended catch-alls — "such other entities serviced by the Company" and, after a long enumerated list, "and other related services" — which is the classic general-versus-specific problem, and "including but not limited to" makes the list's limiting force contestable. The scope of the noncompete turns entirely on how far those catch-alls reach.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Business" drives Article V(a), 1.4 Company Technology, 1.6 Core Business and 8.2(c), and V(d) swaps it for "Core Business" on an 8.4 termination, so any looseness here propagates; 1.5 also refers to "Parent... their Business," though Business is defined only by reference to the Company. That interlocking use raises but does not itself create a contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard incorporation of the Internal Revenue Code as amended; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: "Code" appears nowhere else in the operative text — a defined term with no use is a minor drafting orphan rather than a genuine inconsistency, and it cannot conflict with anything.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Known to the Employee as a consequence of or through the Employee's employment" is a vague boundary — it can be read to sweep in general knowledge and ideas the Employee brought with him, and "ideas, concepts, know-how" are unpatentable subject matter assigned wholesale.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 4.1 requires assignment of items "conceived, developed or acquired during the Employment Term," which is a different (and in places broader) trigger than "known to the Employee," so the definition and its only operative user do not line up exactly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "All information, in whatever form, regarding Parent, the Company their Business and their clients" is unbounded and has a missing comma; the ten enumerated categories follow "without limitation," so their limiting force on the general opening words is contestable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.1's exceptions (public domain, rightful receipt, legal compulsion) do the work of cabining the definition, so the pairing is reasonably coherent; the reference to Parent's "Business" is loose because Business is defined only as the Company's activities.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The (b)(ii) test is close to self-defeating as written — new-contract revenue must exceed "the sum of (A) one percent of Ajuba's... gross revenue and (B) the scheduled first-year gross revenue for such new contract," i.e. must exceed itself plus 1% — and the (a)/(b) structure with "either" leaves it unclear whether the limbs are cumulative or alternative. Those are nameable textual defects with real consequences.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Core Business is the substituted scope in Article V(d) for a Section 8.4 termination, so the arithmetic defect directly infects the enforceable reach of the noncompete; limb (a) also appears to swallow the whole of "Business" as defined in 1.2, making the 1% carve-outs in (b) redundant.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The measuring point is "the date of termination of this Agreement," while limb (c) speaks of contact "while an employee" — Agreement termination and employment termination are not the same event, and "actively sought" and "material contact" are soft boundaries.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article VIII terminates the Employee's employment rather than the Agreement (9.7 expressly contemplates surviving provisions), so the trigger date used in this definition does not map cleanly onto the termination machinery it depends on.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional GAAP-based EBITDA definition with a designated tiebreaker; the only softness is the shift between lowercase "fiscal year" and the defined "Fiscal Year."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is measured on Ajuba's audited statements, while 2.2(b) pays the Bonus within thirty days of receipt of Parent's audited financial statements — a small mismatch of reference documents between the definition and the clause that uses it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite: a three-year term subject to early termination under Article VIII.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It runs to "the third anniversary of this Agreement" whereas 8.1 says "the third anniversary of the Effective Date"; the two are almost certainly the same date, but the Effective Date itself is left blank in the preamble.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Defines a calendar year with a unilateral-sounding escape ("or such other 12-month period as may constitute Ajuba's fiscal year at any time hereafter"), which allows the measuring period for bonuses to be moved.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: That flexibility interacts with the fixed annual EBITDA targets in 2.2(b), which assume calendar years, but nothing squarely contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A named corporation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parent is used in 1.5, 1.7, Article V(b), 8.4(b) and 9.9 consistently; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A boilerplate omnibus definition; "other entity" is a catch-all but a wholly conventional one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Used only in 2.1(b) (board service with a Person not in competition); no tension with anything else.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Geographically definite — the United States, its territories and protectorates, and India — with no soft edge worth arguing about.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It plugs into Article V(a) and, with the three-year-plus Restricted Period, into V(e)'s reasonableness acknowledgment and Article VII's blue-pencil sentence; that is a tension about enforceability rather than a textual conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The words are arithmetically clear but produce a period commencing at signature and ending three years after the end of a three-year term — a six-year restraint whose length is the sort of thing parties fight over, though not because the words are ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V(e) has the Employee acknowledging the restrictions are "reasonable in scope and duration" while Article VII expressly anticipates a court finding them overbroad and modifying them; 9.8 also carves out a separate Non-Competition Agreement of even date whose period may differ.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Long but mostly definite; the softness lies in "such other legally permissible and proper duties... consistent with Employee's services provided to the Company prior to the date hereof or with Employee's position," and in the self-executing sentence that Schedule 2.1 "shall be deemed to have been amended" upon consolidation, elimination or outsourcing of 8.4(a) functions.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It says the Employee reports directly to the Board, while Schedule 2.1 says he "[r]eports to the Chairman of the Board"; and the deemed-amendment sentence is designed to neutralise 8.4(a)'s material-diminution Good Reason trigger, which is exactly the kind of interaction a court has to reconcile.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The EBITDA step-up is genuinely ambiguous — "if Ajuba's EBITDA equals or exceeds $3.5 million" names no measurement year, and "retroactive to the first business day of the year following the Fiscal Year in which such EBITDA was achieved" is internally awkward (retroactivity to a future year's start).
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The clause gives an $18,800 Allowance expressly "in lieu of receiving health, dental and other benefits," while 2.2(c) entitles the Employee to participate in all benefit plans made available to senior executives or employees generally — the two provisions pull in opposite directions on benefits.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The table gives discrete EBITDA points rather than bands, so it does not say what is payable at, say, $3.9 million, and "shall be eligible to receive" sits uneasily with the mandatory payment sentence that follows.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The FY2007 proviso conditions payment on remaining employed "through the entire Employment Term" unless terminated under 8.3 or 8.4, while 8.2 and 8.5 flatly deny "any other bonus or other compensation pursuant to Section 2... for either the prior or current year" — the interaction of these bonus-forfeiture rules is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Entitled to participate in all employee benefit plans" followed by a right to modify or discontinue them "at the sole discretion of the Company" is a familiar construction, but the entitlement and the discretion are in tension within the same short paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(a) gives the Allowance expressly "in lieu of receiving health, dental and other benefits afforded to Ajuba US employees," which is hard to reconcile with an entitlement to participate in all plans available to employees generally; 8.2, 8.3, 8.4 and 8.5 then cut off plan participation after termination.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Substantially similar to the D&O Policy maintained by the Company immediately prior to the date hereof" is a soft benchmark, but a common and workable one.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: A failure here would be a breach of "the compensation and benefit provisions of Section 2.2" and so a Good Reason trigger under 8.4(c); that is coherent rather than contradictory.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Net sales" is undefined, "Samii" is an unexplained name, the condition "as of the Payment Date (as defined below)" uses a term defined only later and monthly, and the closing sentence switches to the conditional "would no longer be payable" — several nameable soft spots in a payment formula.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.3 and 8.4 both promise the Reorganization Bonus "in accordance with Section 2.2(e)" — but 2.2(e) is this commission clause and the Reorganization Bonus lives in 2.2(f), so the cross-reference machinery around this subsection is broken.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "When and if the Company's UK office is shut down and the Company's Novi office is restructured" is a condition whose satisfaction Schedule I defines only partly, and the subsection label is garbled ("(f"); it also describes Schedule I as setting out "specific cost savings" and "a reasonable risk assessment."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 8.3 and 8.4 preserve the Reorganization Bonus "in accordance with Section 2.2(e)" — a mis-citation to the commissions clause — and Schedule I disclaims any representation or warranty about the very cost savings this clause says the Schedule "sets forth," so the pieces do not fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Reasonable out-of-pocket expenses" subject to "Company policies" is standard and readily applied.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Breach of 2.3 is a listed Good Reason under 8.4(c), which is a coherent linkage; nothing contradicts it.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: The exceptions harmonise with the broad 1.5 definition, and 9.7 lets the obligation survive termination; no conflict located.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Engage in any activity which is in competition with the Business," "directly or indirectly" and "or otherwise" after a list of capacities are all open-textured, and the reach of the covenant depends wholly on the contestable 1.2 definition of Business.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: V(d) replaces "Business" with "Core Business" on an 8.4 termination, V(e) declares the restraint reasonable while Article VII anticipates judicial modification, and 9.8 preserves a separate Non-Competition Agreement of even date — several places where this covenant's operative scope must be reconciled with other text.

judgments.reasoning_cat2: It applies for the whole Restricted Period without the V(d) narrowing, and its reference to persons employed "during the six months prior to termination of Employee's employment" sits alongside the 1.7 Customer definition's own six-month look-back measured from termination of the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Disability test (120 days in any 240-day period, "substantially failed to perform his essential duties") is workable, but the paragraph says the Company "shall continue to be liable for the Base Salary" and then "except as expressly set forth in this Section 8.3" negates other compensation — a self-referential exception that is hard to apply.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The forfeiture is triggered by violating "the terms of this Agreement" without any materiality or cure qualifier, and it releases the Company from obligations "under the Severance Agreement" — an instrument bearing no defined name anywhere in the document; the sentence also trails off with a comma.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Release is called the "Release" and severance is actually promised by Section 8.4 of the Employment Agreement, so the undefined "Severance Agreement" has to be matched to one of them; this also cuts against ¶1's carve-out preserving the Employee's claims to compel payment.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duties bullet listing advisory responsibilities with an "including... and other strategic partnership arrangements" catch-all; broad but plainly advisory in character.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 says the Employee reports directly to the Board while this bullet has him advising the Chairman and the Board, and 2.1 makes the Schedule control over the Bylaws — consistent enough, but the reporting lines across the Schedule and 2.1 are not uniform.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The bullet assigns responsibility for "Finance/Accounting/Cash Management (including Ajuba US and all subsidiaries)" with an "including" list whose reach is open, but the wording itself is intelligible.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4(a) expressly declares that consolidation, elimination or outsourcing of cash management, accounting and sales and marketing is not a material diminution, and 2.1 deems the Schedule amended in that event — so the very functions this bullet confers can be stripped without breach, a tension a court would have to resolve.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single flat statement of reporting lines; nothing ambiguous in it.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is subject to 2.1's deemed-amendment sentence and to 8.4's acknowledgment that the Employee's title may be reduced to Senior Vice President after year one, which would be hard to square with all India employees continuing to report to him.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four words, entirely definite on their own terms.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 states that the Employee "shall report directly to the Board (or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)," while this Schedule says he reports to the Chairman — and 2.1 provides the Schedule controls over the Bylaws but says nothing about a conflict with 2.1 itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple quarterly attendance obligation; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coexists with 9.14's recusal requirement and with 2.1's reporting duty without contradiction.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Completion is defined by an objective "last to occur" test tied to named individuals and a dated lease, which is unusually precise; the cost figures are labelled estimates and the itemised list sums correctly.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) describes Schedule I as setting out "the specific cost savings for each action," but this Schedule gives only operating-cost estimates and later disclaims any warranty of savings, so the bonus condition and the Schedule are not perfectly aligned.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The heading and 2.2(f) speak of "restructure," but the text defines completion solely by termination of a named lease, and it also slips into speaking of "closure" of the Novi office — a shift of concept within one paragraph.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) conditions $200,000 on the Novi office being "restructured" in accordance with this Schedule, so whether lease termination alone earns the bonus depends on reading the two together; the risk-assessment sentence is also qualified by the disclaimer that follows.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear disclaimer that the figures are good-faith estimates only, though it references "Contemplated Transactions (as defined in the Stock Purchase Agreement dated June __, 2005)" — an undated, unattached instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) treats Schedule I as "set[ting] forth the specific cost savings for each action and a reasonable risk assessment," while this paragraph disclaims any representation as to actual savings — the operative bonus clause and the Schedule characterise the same content differently.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single allocation sentence, unambiguous in scope and in who bears the cost.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It places the closure costs on Ajuba even though 2.2(f) has Ajuba India paying the Reorganization Bonus and the Company as a whole benefiting; a minor allocation mismatch, not a genuine conflict.
